'''Leslie Colin Woods''' (6 December 1922 – 15 April 2007) was a New Zealand mathematician.

== Early life and education ==
Woods was born on 6 December 1922 in  Reporoa, New Zealand.<ref name="MacTutor">{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=J J |last2=Robertson |first2=E F |title=Leslie Woods (1922 - 2007) |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Woods/ |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive |publisher=University of St Andrews, Scotland |access-date=8 January 2021}}</ref> Woods' father was a fisherman.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2007/jun/07/guardianobituaries.obituaries|title=Obituary: Leslie Woods|first1=Garry|last1=Tee|first2=Graeme|last2=Wake|date=7 June 2007|website=the Guardian|accessdate=16 May 2018}}</ref> His surname was originally Woodhead.

His school education was completed in New Zealand, where he attended Seddon Memorial Technical College (where he was Head Boy).<ref name="MCreg">{{cite book|editor1-last=Levens|editor1-first=R.G.C.|title=Merton College Register 1900–1964|date=1964|publisher=Basil Blackwell|location=Oxford|page=397}}</ref> In his autobiography ''Against the Tide: An Autobiographical Account of a Professional Outsider'', he gives credit to his school teachers, including Colin Maloy and G J Park, for kindling his interest in science and encouraging him to take up a career in academia.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gtcgCAAAQBAJ&dq=Cyril+Maloy&pg=PA38|title=Against the Tide: An Autobiographical Account of a Professional Outsider|first=L. C.|last=Woods|date=1 January 2000|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=9781482268751|accessdate=16 May 2018|via=Google Books}}</ref>

In 1940 Woods went on to study at [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]], but left to join the [[Royal New Zealand Air Force]] in December 1941. After completing his training as a pilot he was posted to the Pacific Area in 1943, serving three tours of duty in 1944 and 1945.<ref name="MCreg" />

After the war Woods returned to Auckland University College, taking his MSc in 1945 and a BE in 1947. The following year he matriculated at [[Merton College, Oxford]] on a Rhodes Scholarship; he studied there until 1951, taking a DPhil in 1950, and then, unusually, a first-class BA in Mathematics in 1951.<ref name="MCreg" />

== Academic career == 
Woods was the Nuffield Research Professor of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Technology at Sydney.<ref name="telegraph.co.uk">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1552138/Professor-Les-Woods.html|title=Professor Les Woods|date=20 May 2007|publisher=|accessdate=16 May 2018|via=www.telegraph.co.uk}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of Balliol College, Oxford in 1961 where he researched the theory of magnetically-confined hot plasmas. Woods was professor of mathematics at the University of Oxford from 1970 until his retirement in 1990. <ref name="Theory of Tokamak Transport">{{cite book |last=Woods |first=Leslie |date=2006 |title=Theory of Tokamak Transport |location=Oxford |publisher=Wiley-VCH |isbn=3-527-40625-5 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1943, Woods married Gladys Elizabeth (Betty) Bayley; they had five daughters.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="MCreg" />

Woods died on 15 April 2007 in [[Oxford]].<ref name="MacTutor" />

== Bibliography ==

His notable books include:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/1703757.Leslie_Colin_Woods|title=Leslie Colin Woods|website=www.goodreads.com|accessdate=16 May 2018}}</ref>

* ''The Theory of Subsonic Plane Flow'' (1961)
* ''The Thermodynamics of Fluid Systems'' (1975)
* ''Principles of Magnetoplasma Dynamics'' (1987)
* ''Kinetic Theory of Gases and Magnetoplasmas'' (1993)
* ''Thermodynamic Inequalities with Applications to Gases and Magnetoplasmas'' (1996)
* ''Against the Tide: An Autobiographical Account of a Professional Outsider'' (2000)
* ''Physics of Plasmas'' (2003)
* ''Theory of Tokamak Transport: New Aspects for Nuclear Fusion Reactor Design'' (2006)
